analysis.investment_thesis: City Union Bank is a conservatively managed 120-year-old Tamil Nadu SME lender with consistent profitability and improving liability structure, but an ROE of 11.87% is structurally below my 15% threshold for any leveraged institution. At P/B 1.92x, you are paying a premium for below-average returns on equity.
key_strengths: Consistent net profit growth: INR 760 Cr → INR 1,124 Cr over 3 years (13.9% CAGR), OCF positive all 4 tracked years
Disciplined liability management — institutional borrowings halved from INR 5,312 Cr (FY22) to INR 1,790 Cr (FY25), reducing funding risk
Conservative credit culture focused on South Indian SME/trade finance; forward P/E of 12.54 offers a reasonable entry if growth sustains
key_risks: ROE of 11.87% — the cardinal sin for a bank; compounding equity below 12% means capital is being destroyed relative to cost
Revenue grew only 6.3% CAGR over 3 years — modest for a bank operating in a high-growth Indian economy with structural credit demand
Finance costs grew 17.2% CAGR (INR 2,188 Cr → INR 3,518 Cr), outpacing revenue growth, compressing net interest margins
red_flags: ROE of 11.87% fails my 15% minimum — a bank trading at 1.92x book should be earning well above this
Operating CF was volatile (INR 1,166 Cr → INR 436 Cr → INR 1,128 Cr), reflecting lumpy working capital cycles typical of concentrated SME portfolios
analysis.detailed_analysis:
City Union Bank has a genuine franchise — 120 years of operating history, deep roots in Tamil Nadu trade and SME finance, and a conservative culture that has kept it out of the headline NPA scandals that have plagued Indian banking. Net profit has grown reliably, and the reduction in higher-cost borrowings from INR 5,312 Cr to INR 1,790 Cr is a positive structural shift. The forward P/E of 12.54 is not demanding by Indian banking standards.

But Munger's inversion is clear: why is ROE only 11.87% for a bank with this vintage and franchise? Banks are inherently leveraged — if the core business doesn't earn 15%+ ROE, the margin of safety against a credit cycle or rate shock evaporates quickly. P/B of 1.92x is not cheap for sub-12% equity returns. Revenue growing at 6.3% CAGR while finance costs grow at 17.2% suggests NIM compression is a structural headwind, not a temporary one. A decent bank at a full price — monitor but do not add.
